selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main warning at the beginning of the passage about focusing only on this worldly life?
questions.answer: It turns a person’s enjoyment into deep sorrow.

questions.question: What does the first man’s happiness tell us about his expectations?
questions.answer: He expects reunion, not total loss.

questions.question: How does the second man try to deal with his sadness?
questions.answer: He attaches himself to one guest and tries to use that person to ease his pain.

questions.question: How should this truth affect a believer’s fear of death?
questions.answer: It should reduce fear and build courage.

questions.question: What attitude is the reader told to have toward the grave?
questions.answer: The reader is told not to fear it blindly but to face it with courage.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the movement of human life toward its end?
questions.answer: It says the movement continues and even speeds up.

questions.question: Why does the passage reject the thought, “I am like everyone else”?
questions.answer: Because people only stay with you up to the grave, so that idea cannot truly comfort you after death.

questions.question: What details from creation are mentioned to prove deep order in the world?
questions.answer: The layered beauty of living things and the disciplined movement of the earth are mentioned.

questions.question: According to the passage, under whose command do such major events occur?
questions.answer: They occur by the command of Allah, who is All-Wise and All-Compassionate.

questions.question: How are people of shirk and people of gratitude treated differently at the end?
questions.answer: People of shirk are driven to Hell, while grateful people are called to Paradise.

questions.question: What big idea is taught by the phrase about limiting one’s sight to this world?
questions.answer: If a person cares only about this life, something that could feel sweet becomes painful.

questions.question: Why does the first man think about that place so much?
questions.answer: Because the people he loves are there and he hopes to join them.

questions.question: Why is the second man’s comfort weak and incomplete?
questions.answer: Because he tries to replace many lost friends with one passing companion.

questions.question: What truth about the grave is given to the nafs?
questions.answer: The truth is that loved ones, especially the Prophet and others, are already beyond it.

questions.question: What common excuse about society and earning a living is directly challenged?
questions.answer: The excuse that worldly struggle makes spiritual concern unrealistic.

questions.question: Which realities stay fixed no matter the era?
questions.answer: Death and separation stay fixed, and human weakness and need remain too.

questions.question: What does the “guesthouse of the world” image suggest about human life here?
questions.answer: It suggests that life here is temporary and we are only guests.

questions.question: If the world is ordered, what should we understand about ourselves?
questions.answer: We should understand that we are not outside that order or without purpose.

questions.question: For believing people, how can material loss become something better?
questions.answer: It can turn into lasting reward like charity.

questions.question: How can these painful events relate to believers’ sins?
questions.answer: They can wipe away sins caused by not being thankful enough.

questions.question: What happens to worldly pleasure when a person sees only this world and nothing beyond it?
questions.answer: That pleasure changes into painful sorrow.

questions.question: Why does the first man welcome the news of departure?
questions.answer: Because departure means joining the people he loves.

questions.question: Why is his attempt to find comfort not enough?
questions.answer: Because it cannot truly replace all those he thinks he has lost.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to the few still left behind?
questions.answer: They will also go there.
